questions.q: Identify the two supporting characters in the poem "पैक दकस दकस वपंज उघा फुगरह" and state one defining action for each.
questions.a: The two supporting characters are the maid (पैक) and the narrator's wife (चये). The maid's defining action is her persistent refusal to learn reading/writing despite the narrator's efforts (e.g., saying "मैं तो नहीं पढ़ी" and later "पैक कहती है: रे दकन घ कसन दजस फनु हकज"). The wife's defining action is her pragmatic intervention urging the narrator to teach the maid practically ("पैक चखह% रे फदरस >वबस गकस] नस[क्क"). A wrong answer that lists the narrator as a supporting character reveals confusion between protagonist and supporting roles; listing only the maid misses the wife's crucial thematic function.

questions.q: Explain in your own words why the maid says "डयड्कस इज टज फजस" (keep the pen on the ear) and what this reveals about her worldview.
questions.a: The maid says this to reject the narrator's academic approach to literacy — she sees the pen behind the ear as a performative symbol of educated status that doesn't translate to survival skills. Her worldview values tangible labor ("गजस कक<+स दके लज<सक") over symbolic literacy. A wrong answer interpreting this as mere stubbornness or ignorance misses the class critique: she's asserting that her illiteracy is a rational response to a system where literacy doesn't guarantee dignity or food security.

questions.q: Apply the PEEL structure to write a 4-sentence analysis of how the wife's dialogue in the final stanza ("पैक चखह% रे फदरस >वबस गकस...") functions as a narrative pivot.
questions.a: **Point:** The wife's dialogue shifts the poem from abstract idealism to material pragmatism. **Evidence:** She says "पैक चखह% रे फदरस >वबस गकस] नस[क्क" (Paik says: you keep doing big work, sister) and urges practical literacy ("पैक] रे पढ़ ले") tied to real needs like reading letters when the daughter-in-law is away. **Explanation:** Unlike the narrator's philosophical "डयड्कस इज टज फजस", the wife frames literacy as a tool for navigating patriarchal household crises — the maid must read letters to maintain family connections. **Link:** This pivot exposes the narrator's reformism as detached from the lived reality of women's domestic labor. A weak answer would only paraphrase the dialogue without contrasting the two women's approaches to literacy.

questions.q: Analyze how the maid's physical description ("पैक लकुंज ध ्म+ध गस% ककसा-हकसालस ज[करक गस") and her labor ("पैक पपसक;कस दकस दकस पजरघ दजस तकरह गस") function as a symbolic counterpoint to the narrator's intellectual labor.
questions.a: The maid's "clean" (लकुंज) appearance despite handling "dirt" (ककसा-हकसालस) symbolizes dignity in manual labor, while her managing "four corners" (पपसक;कस दकस दकस) of the household represents holistic, embodied knowledge. The narrator's intellectual labor (reading/writing) is fragmented and performative ("डयड्कस इज टज फजस"), whereas the maid's labor integrates body, space, and social reproduction. A wrong answer treating the description as mere realism misses the symbolic structure: the poem contrasts two epistemologies — bookish vs. embodied — with the maid embodying the latter's completeness.

questions.q: Evaluate the criticism that the poem ultimately reinforces the narrator's savior complex by making the maid's illiteracy a project for his enlightenment. Defend or refute using textual evidence.
questions.a: Refute: The poem subverts the savior complex through the maid's agency — she rejects the narrator's pedagogy ("मैं तो नहीं पढ़ी") and only engages when the wife reframes literacy as *her* need ("पैक] रे पढ़ ले... डयड्क्के इम लनसलक नकसख"). The final image — "डयड्क्के इम लनसलक नकसख" (don't ever go to the daughter-in-law's house) — centers the maid's survival strategy, not the narrator's teaching. A wrong answer accepting the criticism overlooks how the narrative structure gives the maid the last word (her laughter "पैक पकी गस" and practical wisdom), decentering the narrator's reformist ego.

questions.q: Create a 4-line dialogue poem between the maid and a modern gig-worker (delivery person) where both articulate why formal literacy feels irrelevant to their survival. Use the maid's voice from the poem as inspiration.
questions.a:
**Maid:** "अककसर सजखके पेट भरे ना, रोटी ककसका भरे"  
**Gig-worker:** "ऐप पढ़के दकसका भला, रेट दकसका ना बढे"  
**Maid:** "चिट्ठी पढ़के बऊ लटौ, यहीं मेरो हकज"  
**Gig-worker:** "ओटोपी दकसका चलाउ, रास्तो मेरो पचहानो"  
A poor answer would write generic complaints about education without anchoring each line in the specific material logic of their labor (the maid's household management, the gig-worker's algorithmic navigation) as the poem does.
